text:
morgan: quick sync — noticed preemptible credit ledger diverging from operator leases after a force-evict/backfill window this morning. details below, want to align on where reconciliation should live.

riley: ugh, saw that alert. scenario?

morgan: tenant A had reserved 10 slots, used 6, then we force-evicted a noisy job and backfilled with ephemeral workloads. operator freed leases but the credit-service still counted them until the next periodic reconcile. gap ~ 4 credits for ~7m.

sam: is this the same window where autoscaler admitted ephemeral bursts directly into burst-lane bypassing reservation accounting?

morgan: yes. admission path is fine, but operator and credit-service have different sources of truth. operator marks lease released immediately; credit-service relies on events that sometimes get coalesced/filtered.

jia: can we make credit-service subscribe to operator lease events instead of event-sourced coalesced deltas?

alex: subscribing helps but then operator->credit ordering matters. if operator emits release then immediate reassign, we might see a transient negative. need idempotent ops.

riley: two high-level options: 1) move reconciliation into operator (single source of truth) 2) keep credit-service authoritative but tighten event guarantees and add a lease-version field. tradeoffs?

sam: operator-authoritative simplifies correctness but couples autoscaler operator and billing/credits logic. that smells risky for long-term: makes operator bigger and harder to maintain.

jia: agree. if credit-service remains authoritative we should add lease_hints: {lease_id, version, tenant, seq} and operator should attach seq on release. credit-service can reject stale messages and do faster reconciliation when gaps detected.

morgan: also worried about race during backfill: operator might preempt a tenant lease and immediately allocate to a burst tenant. credit-service shouldn't charge the preempted tenant for that window. we need clear semantics: release timestamp determines charge cutover.

alex: yeah, define charge boundary = operator event timestamp for RELEASE. credit-service uses that timestamp when computing usage. events must carry monotonic wall-clock or hybrid logical clock to avoid reorder problems across AZs.

riley: what about short-term fix: make the reconcile frequency shorter and add a reactive reconcile when operator detects large-scale eviction? buys time while we design protocol.

morgan: short-term +1. also throw an alert if ledger delta > threshold within 15m.

sam: longer term we should spec the operator->credit protocol: schema (lease_id, op, ts, version), semantics for retry, idempotency, and a reconciliation contract. I can draft an RFC.

jia: include at least one flow for partial failure: operator emits event; credit-service ack lost; operator will retry with same version; credit-service must be idempotent. Add a compact tombstone for old leases to prevent unbounded state.

alex: and update admission path to read a fast cache of credit balances from credit-service instead of local operator estimates. reduces mismatch during admission.

riley: risks: increased cross-service coupling and latency on admission if we rely on synchronous calls. mitigation: read-through cache with short TTL + sub-second invalidation via events.

morgan: plan: (1) short-term: reduce reconcile to 1m + add alerting + reactive reconcile on big evictions (2) medium: add lease_version & release_ts to events, make credit-service reject stale events and retry semantics (3) long: RFC to move billing out of event-coalesced model to operator-driven event stream with HL-clock. Sam to draft RFC by EOW.

sam: on it. I'll include sequence diagrams and a proposed event schema.

deploy-bot: monitor: reconcile-lag alert muted -> unmuted after 2026-03-21T09:00:00Z by sam.

morgan: thanks everyone. I'll open a short-term ops ticket for the 1m reconcile and alert thresholds.

riley: thanks — ping if you want help testing the reactive reconcile trigger. :thumbsup:

morgan: will do.
